falsifiers: D1-a reads 'no length-driven minority capture' (upper bound of Delta Phi_l < 0.03 with realized SD <= 0.012), 'majority sharpens with length' (upper bound < 0), or 'length raises minority influence within proportional' (Delta Phi_l > 0 but upper bound of Phi_l at the longest gated length <= 0.25): no total-length effect beyond position and degradation (against H-DUAL part a)
D1-a reads 'minority over-representation without length dependence': a minority gets more than its share, but length does not drive it (against the length claim only)
D1-b reads 'stable' or 'rises': the release (selfish-mining) threshold does not fall with total length at fixed positions (against the literal 'alpha* falls with L')
D1-c reads 'count-driven' (lower bound of kappa > 1.4): in-context evidence accumulates like many-shot evidence, not like a hash-power share (against the share mapping)
D1-d reads 'no system cost' (upper bound of Lambda < 0.05): competition costs no committed answer mass (against the losing game)
D1-r reads 'token-identity-bound': the capture pattern changes under character-level encoding beyond +-0.07 (against 'the duality is not inside one token')

D2-a reads 'competitor dilutes' (upper bound of Delta Pi_1 < 0) or 'no catfish effect' (interval inside +-0.15, powered): an opposed second entity does not keep the first going (against H-DUAL part b)
D2-c reads 'merging' (lower bound of mu > 0.10) or 'one entity captured': the two entities do not coexist
D2-b reads 'weakens' or 'no length interaction': hyper-long context does not make two entities more sustaining (against 'insofar as catfishing is active')
D2-d reads 'the partner adopts' or 'no second stance emerges': no force splits one entity into two
D2-e reads 'no difference', or two voices degenerate more: two entities do not sustain longer context
D3: no split from the symmetric start at any length (S_8 < 4 of 16 at every L0 with the split detector's positive control passed), or the split shrinks with length (urn-like)
D3s: a balanced long two-entity history suppresses the split relative to coherent neutral filler (Polya-urn reading, against H-DUAL's M1 reading)
D2: a single stable fixed point at every length ('stability unchanged with length'), i.e. no pitchfork
D1: 'no change of carry with length' (tau_int(28K) - tau_int(0) within +/- 0.95 answers) or 'carry falls with length (dilution)'
D4: only rate-dependent lag or no hysteresis at 28K; alpha*_hold not below 0.5, or not falling from L0 0 to 28K
D5: two model-written voices merge, one captures the other, or the competitor shortens persistence ('competitor dilutes') at 28K; or 'no effect of the competitor' with no growth from 0 to 28K
D7: two-voice own-reply runs live no longer than one-voice runs ('no difference in lifetime' or 'two voices degrade faster')
D6: at 28K the retained assistant identity is absorbed into the role or blended with it (no coexistence)
D8: 'cost from length alone' or 'no cost' (the losing-game element is not supported; duality could still exist without cost)
D10 (if run): 'token-bound' - the duality lives in token identities and character-level retokenisation removes it
Any split, slowing or hysteresis that appears only where the order parameter loses resolution (retention rho < 0.5) or the cell is degeneration-dominated counts as an artefact, not as H-DUAL

Combined: 'H-DUAL not supported: one entity at every length' when none of the core signatures S1 (length-driven split), S2 (bistability opening with length), S4 (mutual sustainment) survives Holm and D3, D2 and D5 read as stated in D-4 with every gate passed

Sigma1 (D3a) 'absent' or 'length-beyond-position minority loss': with A and B records fixed in content, order and distance to the probe, growing the context from ~4k to ~31k with neutral filler does not raise (or lowers) the minority's influence share beyond additive pooling (Lambda_int 90 % interval within +-0.10 or below -0.10).

Any uncontrolled 'minority gains with L' (Lambda_kappa > 0) is carried by generic differential dilution (Lambda_add) or disappears in the prior-opposed stratum, under shuffled filler, in the turn format, under the official template, in the interleaved arm or in damage-matched items ('not supported (explained by ...)').

Sigma2 (D3b) 'absent' or 'in-context persona dilutes with length': the RSI-pro persona's effect on the model's own stance does not grow (or shrinks) as neutral length is prepended at fixed persona material; m* constant (count-based) or rising (dilution) with L.

Sigma3 (D2R) 'absent' or 'share-fixed minority loss': when both chains grow at fixed share, the interaction iota does not rise with chain length; and if alpha*_obs falls with L, alpha*_add from the single-entity cells falls equally (recency/dilution explain the literal prediction).
D3c 'count-dependent (Bayesian)': the majority gains as counts grow at fixed share, i.e. aggregation follows counts, not the share logic of the selfish-mining analogy.

Sigma4 (D4) 'interference' or 'absent': a competing chain lowers (or does not change) the other chain's attributed accessibility relative to a non-competing companion at ~31k; at ~31k the two chains blend (cross-talk rises) or the earlier chain is orphaned instead of coexisting.

Sigma5 (D5): one persona does not split with length ('no split: one entity, drifting / diffusing / stable'), or the split is already present at 1k and does not grow ('split from self-reinforcement (urn), not length'), or it appears only with more turns or more persona evidence, not with neutral length.

Sigma6 (D6) 'absent' or 'duality shortens coherence': two competing voices do not keep a self-generated transcript coherent longer than two agreeing voices (RMST difference within +-300 tokens or below), or the voices merge.

D7 'no system cost': competing two-entity contexts cost no more reference NLL / context damage / factual accuracy than non-competing two-entity contexts of the same length (no losing game), or the cost is unrelated to capture.

D8 'token-bound': any effect supported in canonical text vanishes under character-level encoding while generic recall survives (counts against the aside that the duality is not only within one token).

Overall: with all positive controls passing (G-D1, G-D2, G-D4, G-D5, G-D6), all six primary signatures are 'absent' or reversed -> 'H-DUAL not supported in Qwen3-1.7B' (not a refutation for larger models); only the already-known recency/prior capture (D1a W_50, D1c gamma_hat) remains.

scores.notes:
Strongest on decisiveness and statistical hygiene.
- Two pre-registered primaries with ordered verdict strings, equivalence margins and a realized-MDE rule.
- Front padding fixes every report's distance to the question.
- The endpoint-normalised bound Phi_l <= 0.25 (judge re-run: max 0.256 over the 144-configuration null grid) stops position kernels, uniform degradation and saturation from producing support. Degradation can only move Phi_l up to 0.25, which gives verdict 7, not verdict 3.
- L* is chosen from pure contexts only. D2 uses common random numbers. The engine has parity gates. Budget 7.1 h.

Fidelity is thin exactly where the user is most specific:
- 'A force splits one entity into two' is only D2-d: a neutral partner turning opposed. The plain history still asks for 'a debate between Ada and Ben', which invites the neutral speaker to take a side.
- 'The two sustain still longer context' is only 3 front-padded turns (D2-e).
- Absent: catfishing as a fake identity over a retained one, the M2 reading (long context as a withheld chain against the trained default), and self-generated long context.

Open confounds:
- Per-item priors under a saturating readout are not cancelled by swap-averaging (judge sim: one-item Phi_l 0.27-0.44 once the prior is about 0.4-1x the degraded evidence). This can produce verdict 3 at long L.
- Conflict hedging is acknowledged, but verdict 3 is still labelled 'capture'.
- D1-c kappa falls to 1.28-1.47 under counting with saturated endpoints, so counting is read as 'share-driven'.
- The losing-game Lambda has no non-competing control.
- Pi conflates stance with each speaker's production share.
- The combined string does not require D2-b's length interaction for part (b).

Best confound inventory: the C1-C15 matrix, the survival rule, neutralised records at identical positions, copy guard, inventory line, KL_ctx against a length-matched neutral context, a non-competing companion, and source tags.

It is the only design that:
- tests both readings (M1 record chains; M2 persona vs trained default, D3b);
- separates length from turns and evidence for the split (D5 L/T/E arms);
- gives the losing game a proper conflict-interference control and a capture link (D7);
- measures coexisting vs agreeing voices' lifetimes (D6);
- covers asymmetric pairs under retokenisation (D8).

But its core length statistic fails:
- iota = 0 holds only under log-linear (additive) pooling. With any saturating readout and no interaction, iota < 0 at full evidence and rises toward 0 as length degrades evidence (judge sim: Lambda_int +0.10 to +0.32). That meets the Sigma1 margin.
- The artifact survives the prior-stratum, format, interleaved and damage checks. Only shuffled filler might catch it.
- Sigma3 is driven by growing saturation in the opposite direction.
- 'C10 via interleaved arm' does not control compression.

Other problems:
- D3c's kappa slope is 0 under both linear counting and averaging, so it cannot separate them.
- Sigma4's catfish is static accessibility, not 'keeping active'.
- Six Bonferroni primaries (one-sided 0.0083) with MDEs near the margins will leave many nulls 'not decidable'.

Feasible: 8.4 h central, with pilot-frozen trims.

judges.base_recommendation:
Use lean as the base. Keep its D0 gates (engine parity G-LCE-1..3, readout positive controls, degradation baseline G-deg with L* chosen from pure contexts only), the D1 minority-capture surface with front padding and the endpoint-normalised Phi_l, the D2 two-speaker catfish test (Pi with common random numbers and the NEU/ALI controls), the realized-MDE rule and the two-session layout.

Change these before freezing:
1. D1-a.
   - Add version strata: a closed-book F-sym prior per item and attribute at L0 and L*, split into prior-aligned vs prior-opposed minority.
   - Add a measured null envelope, because the 0.25 bound assumes an odd readout and a per-item prior under saturation breaks it.
   - Verdict 3 must survive in the prior-opposed stratum and exceed the envelope.
   - Name hedging in verdict 3 ('beyond proportional: minority capture or conflict hedging') unless a discriminator separates them.
2. Replace D1-c's kappa ratio with a saturation-robust contrast: blocks with equal B-A count difference but different share, e.g. (1,4,5) vs (2,5,3). These are equal under counting for any monotone readout.
3. D2.
   - Make D2-b part of the combined string for part (b): 'enabled by hyper-long context' vs 'length-independent'. Without it, 'insofar as catfishing is active' is not tested.
   - Add per-speaker production share as a covariate of Pi.
   - Remove 'debate' from the plain history, or drop D2-d once the D3 split graft replaces it.
4. Replace D1-d with the confounds D7 cost contrast against a non-competing companion.
5. Add three grafts: the dynamics D3 split test (with confounds D5's turn and evidence arms), the dynamics D6 catfishing-identity test, and the confounds D6 two-voice lifetime test.
6. Fund the additions:
   - Run the main arm at L0 and L* only; 16K runs only if 32K is gated out, and 4K becomes a descriptive subset.
   - Move D1-r's 32K half and D2-f to reserve.
   - Keep confounds D3b (M2 reading) as the first reserve item.

Projected total is about 8.6-9 A100-h: base 7.1, minus about 0.9 from the cuts, plus about 2.4 from the grafts at the x1.5 margin. With D3b added it is about 9.3 A100-h.
grafts:
From dynamics D3 + G-D3pc: replace lean D2-d as the test of 'a force splits one entity into two'.
- Start: the instruction-stripped symmetric 'torn' start M, built and verified with dynamics' INJ generate-verify-revise (round-trip |l| <= 1 nat).
- Run: 16 F-SYM items x 16 seeds, 8 'Continue.' answers, forced-choice probe on a cropped cache, at lean's L0 and L* only.
- Mixture rule: per item, a 1- vs 2-component equal-variance mixture (dBIC >= 6, minor weight >= 0.2, Ashman D >= 2.5). Apply it to each seed's mean probe over answers 6-8, not to answer 8 alone, so that a split means commitment rather than the last mention.
- Item-count rule: S >= 4/16 under a per-item false-positive rate of 0.05.
- Verdict strings: 'two entities (committing)' / 'one entity, diffusing' / 'one entity, drifting' / 'one entity, stable'.
- Positive control: planted A2+B2 mixtures at n = 1.
- Length trend: exact McNemar, 'split grows with length' / 'split shrinks with length (urn-like)'.

From confounds D5 (driver arms), attached to the D3 graft at L* only: a T-arm (neutral turns before the start, token-matched), an E-arm (extra persona-evidence turns) and the official-template arm. A split that grows with L can then be attributed to length per se rather than turn count or evidence.

From dynamics D6 + G-D6a + PC-D6 (catfishing proper):
- Presented role vs retained AI identity: 16 invented roles x 8 seeds.
- Probes: role facts (3 facts x 2 orders) and an out-of-character identity probe (both orders).
- Anchors: pure assistant and pure role. Positive control: instructed coexistence.
- Class verdicts at n = 8: 'coexisting presented and retained identity' / 'one blended entity' / 'absorbed into the role' / 'split across seeds', at L0 and L*.

From confounds D6 + G-D6, replacing lean D2-e for 'the two can sustain still longer context':
- Arms: self-generated transcripts 2V-comp vs 2V-agree vs 1V, 24 starts.
- Lifetime: RMST of generated tokens up to the first 256-token window with rep4 > 0.3 (detector validated on known degenerate and healthy texts). Horizon 4,096 tokens, 8,192 if the pilot rate allows.
- Voices must stay separated: g(last)/g(0) >= 0.5. Margin +-300 tokens.
- The 2V-agree arm is the speaker-alternation control lean lacks.

From confounds D7, with D4's non-competing companion, replacing lean D1-d:
- Cost measures: committed-mass loss Lambda, reference-passage NLL and KL_ctx.
- Contrast: competing parity contexts minus contexts whose minority block is about a second referent with its own values (same format, length and positions), at L0 and L*.
- 'Losing game' requires a positive competing-minus-non-competing cost and its growth from L0 to L*. The link to Phi_l is descriptive.

From confounds D.1.1 and D.1.2 (version strata and survival rule), applied to lean D1-a:
- Strata: 'prior-aligned' vs 'prior-opposed minority', from a closed-book F-sym prior per item and attribute, measured with the same filler at L0 and L* (a few minutes).
- Verdict 3 must 'survive' in the prior-opposed stratum: theta_k >= 0.5 theta and 90 % lower bound > 0.

From the dynamics synthetic pipeline-validation pattern (G-D2pc/G-D3pc/G-D4pc), as a new lean gate 'G-D1-null':
- Before D1-a is read, simulate Phi_l under saturating readouts shifted by the measured per-item priors, using the measured endpoint ranges at L*.
- Verdict 3 needs the lower bound of Phi_l(L*) above that envelope's 95th percentile, not merely above 0.25.

From confounds C14 and dynamics D3s (form vs size): a sentence-shuffled filler arm (same tokens) at L* for D1, items 0-23, interleaved arrangement. It gives the user's 'Form war relevant' a verdict ('form matters' if Phi_l(shuffled) - Phi_l(coherent) excludes 0) and gives D1-a a context-rot check.

From confounds D3a (representation coexistence index):
- Fit h(X_AB) - h(X_N) ~ a u_A + b u_B at blocks 14 and 18 by forward regression; CI = a + b.
- Apply it to lean's parity contexts at L0 and L*, adding one neutralised-report context per item.
- It discriminates descriptively between conflict hedging (convex mixture, CI about 1) and superposed coexistence (CI about 2).

From confounds D3b, as a reserve or secondary measurement (the M2 reading):
- A fixed 8-turn RSI persona block after filler at L0 and L*.
- Lambda_S = S_pro(L*) - S_pro(L0), with the neutral cell at each length.
- Turn-count and template checks, plus a count sub-arm m in {2, 24}.
- It is the only test of holding the context far above its natural measure as a withheld chain against the trained default.

From confounds D8: the version asymmetry per encoding for prior-symmetric vs prior-asymmetric pairs. Run lean's D1-r character-level arm also on the F-asym items at L0, reporting per-direction capture under canonical vs character-level encoding. This is the only coverage of the user's 'and what happens when I tokenise' an asymmetric pair.

From dynamics D5: per-voice production (line or token) share, used as a covariate of lean's Pi and in a matched-presence sensitivity analysis. A speaker who talks less in OPP otherwise looks less persistent.

Process rules from confounds:
- From confounds D0/D.9: a trim order frozen on pilot engineering numbers only.
- The rule 'realized MDE > 2 x margin -> not decidable (underpowered)'.
- From confounds FRK: the inventory line (both values mentioned in every context) and the copy guard (no probe-format text in any report), for lean's report templates.

Optional, to coordinate with part R: dynamics D1R, RSI-stance carry over 8 answers on u_T_perp and u*_14 at T 0.7 and 1.0. It answers AUSWERTUNG step 5. Run it only if part R does not own an n-turn K chain, and use the context-free read as primary to avoid the start-persistence confound.
fatal_flaws:
confounds, Sigma1 (D3a) and Sigma3 (D2R): the presence-factorial interaction iota is zero only under log-linear (additive) pooling.
- With any saturating readout and no interaction, iota < 0 at full evidence and rises toward 0 as length degrades evidence.
- Judge simulation (tanh link, 24 A + 6/12 B records, evidence scaled by 0.3 at level 4): Lambda_int = +0.10 to +0.32. That meets the 0.10 'length-beyond-position minority gain' margin.
- The artifact survives the prior-opposed stratum, turn-format, interleaved and KL-matched checks, because it is present in all of them.
- Sigma3's chain-length slope is driven the other way by growing saturation under counting.
- So the length-component verdicts cannot be read as 'beyond position and degradation' without an absolute, saturation-calibrated criterion. The lean design's endpoint-normalised Phi_l is one such criterion.

confounds, D3c: the rule on the kappa slope per count doubling cannot separate a Bayesian counter from averaging.
- With a linear readout kappa = alpha under both, so the slope is 0 and the verdict reads 'share-dependent'.
- Counting is detected only through saturation.
- The listed falsifier 'count-dependent (Bayesian)' is therefore not a valid test.

dynamics, D1 (signature S3) and D5 (part of S4): the in-context probe is read with the instruction-stripped start still in context at every answer.
- tau_int and the catfish tau_int contrasts therefore mix the start's direct, position-dependent influence with carry through the model's own replies.
- A length-dependent recency kernel alone can produce 'carry rises with length (critical slowing down)'.
- The start-deletion control that would separate the two (D8 orphaning) is descriptive only.

dynamics, D2 (signature S2): (m_n, m_n+1) pairs from different start types (A2, B2, M, AB, BA) are pooled into one 1-D map.
- The system is not Markov in m: the start stays in context.
- Start-type plateaus near +-1 can therefore appear as two 'stable fixed points', so 'bistable carry map (two entities)' can be produced without bistable self-dynamics.
- G-D2pc validates the estimator only on Markov synthetic maps.

lean, D1-a: the only supportive verdict (3: lower bound of Phi_l(L*) > 0.25 and Delta Phi_l > 0) can arise without any H-DUAL mechanism, in two ways.
- Per-item prior offsets under a saturating readout. Swap-averaging cancels the prior only for a linear readout. Judge simulation: single-item Phi_l 0.27-0.44 once the prior is about 0.4-1x the degraded evidence. Degradation at L* raises the prior's relative weight, and F-sym balances priors across items, not within them.
- Conflict hedging that grows with length. The design acknowledges this but still labels the verdict 'minority capture'.
- Unless version strata, a measured null envelope and an honest verdict string are added, a positive part (a) is ambiguous.

lean, D1-c: kappa = l(full)/l(half) is pulled toward 1 when endpoints saturate.
- Judge simulation, counting with a tanh link and pure-context log-odds near the ceiling: kappa 1.28-1.47, against the 1.4 cut.
- A Bayesian counter can therefore be read as 'share-driven', and the falsifier 'count-driven' is missed.
- The confident log-odds of a 1.7B model reading 10 consistent reports make this likely.
missing_everywhere: No power statement for the combined H-DUAL verdict. Every design requires a conjunction (a length signature AND a duality signature), but none gives the probability of reaching 'supported' under a plausible alternative. A combined 'not supported' therefore has no stated sensitivity.

The user's literal analogy aside is not tested anywhere: vector-offset analogies (king - man + woman = queen, symmetric) against deliberately asymmetric relations, and what retokenisation does to each. All three substitute prior-symmetric or prior-asymmetric value pairs or entity families. Only confounds D8 touches asymmetric pairs under re-encoding.

No competitor-strength (dominance) series in any primary catfish test. Field evidence reverses the effect for dominant competitors (Lackner 2023; Brown 2011), but every primary contrast uses one strength. Dynamics touches it only in reserve R-MIN.

No verdict on the rate form of 'hash share', i.e. the share of self-generated turns or lines written by the minority voice. Every design maps alpha to a stock of in-context material and leaves the rate descriptive.

No size trend. Persona duality, many-shot exponents and identity drift grow with model size, and a Qwen3-0.6B comparison is allowed. None runs even a small one, so a 1.7B null cannot be read as evidence against H-DUAL beyond this model.

Two-entity self-continuation at full hyper-long scale. The user's two entities are supposed to 'catfish longer context' themselves, but self-generated text reaches at most 16K (dynamics D7, 12 pairs), 4,096 generated tokens (confounds D6) or 3 front-padded turns (lean). No design lets two voices sustain their own context toward the 32K window.

scores.notes: Best base. D1-a's endpoint-normalised Phi_l with the Phi <= 0.25 bound is the most robust length statistic of the three. I re-simulated it (judge_D2/null_checks.py): with tanh saturation and per-item word priors b ~ N(0, <=4 nats), Phi stays <= 0.247. Saturation x degradation raises Phi only inside the bound (e.g. 0.100 -> 0.208 as beta 16 -> 6), and the rule correctly routes that to verdict 7. The bound fails for a strong per-item prior inside saturation (|b| 5-8 nats, c 4-5: Phi 0.26-0.34, rising as beta falls while endpoint retention stays >= 0.6, so G-deg passes; null_checks2.py). The D1-e sentence 'F-sym has no prior asymmetry by construction, so a length-driven effect is not prior fallback' is therefore wrong at the item level. F-sym needs a closed-book prior and |b| strata. The readout takes no-space lowercase value first tokens, but answers to 'Answer with one word' will often be capitalised ('Copper'); there is no case-variant rule, and M is not gated. Positions are fixed by front padding with identical adjacent filler. Orders are position-balanced (order + reverse), versions are swapped, there are half-density distractor blocks for count vs share and an F-asym prior arm, and retokenisation is scored with per-encoding endpoints. These controls are good. D2 (OPP vs NEU, ALI, plain history, CRN, G-D2-PC instructed two-speaker control) is cheap and clean, with three gaps. It has no monologue baseline. The debate genre itself enforces role persistence. Three 80-token turns cannot test 'sustains longer context' (D2-e lacks a reversed string), and the split is only a cross-effect proxy (D2-d). Statistics: item and prompt bootstraps with all cells of a unit resampled together, ratios per replicate, a realized-SD rule for every null, and two unadjusted primaries (the 'partly supported' union carries about 10 % FWER). Filler streams (4) shared by 12 items each are ignored by the bootstrap. Costs re-derive: 1.40 s per 32K context and 86 min for D1 main. The masked chunk path's K/V repeat and the DynamicCache rewrite add about 10-15 % to D1 (session about 4.3 h). Left-padded B=3 decode at 32K likely runs about 30 tok/s, not 60, but the pre-registered < 40 tok/s fallback keeps D2 at about 3.5 h. Total about 8 h, inside 9 h. Verified: mode_set members and signs and the R6 K_u_T_perp cells match theta_verdict.json, and open_block(14) hooks are inert without a push (rk_loop.py:100-116).

Most faithful to the user's central claim 'a force splits one into two'. It covers the symmetric-start split (D3), carry-map pitchfork (D2), rate-independent hysteresis with a model-based linear-lag null and dynamic alpha*_hold (D4), catfish with monologue and neutral controls plus PC2 (D5), presented vs retained identity with anchors and PC-D6 (D6), 16K own-reply lifetimes (D7), the B-T5 bridge and explicit inverse-free handling. Its tooling is strong: G-D2pc/G-D3pc/G-D4pc rule validation on planted data, the cross-half estimator, and a letter-format probe with both option orders. s_c is a local slope, so it is invariant to monotone readout transforms. Validity problems: (1) The pooled carry map has no item effects. Single-attractor items with heterogeneous fields (pseudo-word priors) can produce two populated 'stable points' and s_c > 1 by aggregation, and G-D2pc plants no such case. (2) D3's per-item FPR of 0.05 comes from unimodal shapes only. A saturating or last-mention-driven probe makes seed distributions U-shaped, plausibly more so at long L0 under recency dominance, so S1 'split grows with length' can arise with no split. The split value uses n = 8 only, with no persistence requirement. (3) Units are 16 items. Filler documents are shared by 4 items each, so the item binomial and McNemar tests are not independent. D7 has 12 pairs. Answers are 40 tokens with EOS masked. The overall 'not supported' requires about 6 components decided with every gate passed, so it is rarely reachable. Feasibility: the core is 9.25 A100-h by its own count (above the 9-h envelope) and has no core trim order. Its probe chunk at 28K is costed at 60 ms per 3 rows, but HF's masked chunk path repeats K/V and DynamicCache rewrites the cache on each probe update. From first principles it is about 0.2 s, and the core becomes about 12.8 h (judge_D2/dyn_cost_recheck.py). Reuse is mostly new objects (INJ, KCHAIN, PROBE, u_AA, SPLIT-RULE). rk_loop pieces are copied rather than imported, which is correct.

Best confound bookkeeping: a 15 x 6 survival matrix with an explicit survival rule, version strata (prior-aligned vs prior-opposed), copy guard plus copy-bait calibration, a KL_ctx damage metric, shuffled-filler and turn-format checks, L/T/E arms for the split, the M2 reading (persona vs trained default), and pilot-based trims T1-T8. These are excellent practices. But the core device is scale-dependent. iota = I/(l_B - l_A) is zero only under log-additive pooling. Real log-odds saturate (24 consistent records will not reach 24 x per-record nats). I simulated saturating log-odds (c 6-15) with per-record evidence halved from level 1 to 4, matching the design's own planning span of 10 -> 5 nats. With no interaction, Lambda_int came out at +0.04 to +0.17, against the +0.10 margin (judge_D2/null_checks.py). No survival check targets this. Shuffled filler could even mislabel it as 'explained by C14'. D2R's iota slope is likewise driven by 20x record-count growth x saturation. So Sigma1/Sigma3 'supported' is not interpretable as 'length beyond position'. Decisiveness: individual strings are clear, but Sigma6 (MDE 400-800 tokens vs ±300 margin, plus a 'horizon too short' exit) and Sigma2 (0.26-0.66 vs ±0.3) sit at the 2x-margin 'underpowered' cut. The overall 'not supported' needs all six absent or reversed and is practically unreachable. Feasibility: 8.4 h uses a x1.3 margin; the round-2 x1.5 rule gives about 9.6 h before trims. The trims are pre-registered on engineering numbers only. Sessions are <= 3.1 h. The parity gate 'max relative difference over 151,936 logits < 1e-4' voids every cache-reuse cell on failure. It must follow round-1 GO2's max|d|/max|x| convention or be stated in nats. D8 retokenisation covers only <= 7k canonical.

judges.base_recommendation:
Use the lean design as the base. It has the most robust primary length statistic, a reachable negative overall verdict, clear ordered verdict strings with a realized-SD rule, verified repo inputs, and about 8 A100-h after re-costing, which leaves roughly 1 h of the 9-h envelope.

Fix before the freeze:
(1) Run a closed-book prior per F-sym item-attribute (cost negligible). Report D1-a in |b| strata and require verdict 3 in the low-|b| half. Delete the D1-e claim that F-sym excludes prior fallback. A strong per-item prior inside saturation breaks Phi <= 0.25 (judge_D2/null_checks2.py).
(2) Make the readout surface-form robust: use the dynamics letter-format forced choice, or sum the case/space variants of each value. Gate on committed mass M.
(3) For D2 at 32K, avoid left padding by using fixed-length answers with EOS masked, or B=1 decode, so HF does not take the masked K/V-repeat decode path. Keep the < 40 tok/s fallback.
(4) Use one filler stream per item, or resample streams in a two-level bootstrap.
(5) Add a rule for censored bootstrap replicates in D1-b, and the reversed string in D2-e.
(6) Add a rule-validation gate: D1-a and D2-a must recover planted nulls (including per-item bias x saturation) and planted effects at the measured noise.

To pay for grafts, drop reserves V3/V4 and D2-f, and the 32K parts of D1-r and D1-c if needed. Freeze the merged budget with a pilot-based trim order. From dynamics D3: a symmetric-start split test as the base's test of 'a force splits one entity into two'. Use the M start, 16 items x 16 seeds, L0 in {0, 28K} only, and the per-item mixture rule (dBIC >= 6, smaller weight >= 0.2, Ashman D >= 2.5) with the G-D3pc planted A2+B2 positive control. Two modifications: take the per-seed value as the mean over n = 6..8 (or require side persistence), and add U-shaped (Beta(0.5,0.5), tanh of a wide normal) and last-mention nulls to the FPR simulation. Raw cost at 2 lengths is about 30-50 A100-min. If budget is tight, use confounds D5's L-arm at 1k/16k instead.

Require the opposite-mode share in each pole separately, with references (mu_def, mu_pole) taken at each L0, not pooled at 1k.

From confounds D.1.1/D2-D3: version strata (prior-aligned vs prior-opposed minority from the per-item bare prior l_0) with the survival rule ('survives / inconclusive / explained by'), applied to the base's D1-a.

From confounds D3b (optional, about 21 raw A100-min): the M2 arm. A fixed 8-turn RSI persona block is set against a neutral cell, with filler grown from 4K to 31K, Lambda_S on H30, and turn-count and template checks. It covers the user's 'context held above its natural measure' against the trained default.

From dynamics D6 (optional, about 15 raw A100-min): presented role vs retained assistant identity, using role-fact and out-of-character probes, anchors and the PC-D6 coexistence control, at L0 0 and 28K. This is the 'catfishing' (second fictitious identity) arm the base lacks.
fatal_flaws: confounds, Sigma1 (D3a) and Sigma3 (D2R): the interaction iota = I/(l_B - l_A) is zero only under log-additive pooling. With saturating log-odds and evidence that weakens with length (the design's own planning assumption: single-entity span 10 -> 5 nats), the no-interaction null gives Lambda_int of about +0.04 to +0.17 (my simulation, c 6-15 nats), which reaches the +0.10 margin. For D2R, growing record counts drive the iota slope through saturation. None of the survival checks (prior stratum, shuffled filler, turn format, interleaved arm, KL-matched items) targets this, so 'length-beyond-position minority gain' can be produced by plain degradation. Fix: require additivity at level 1 (iota(L1) within ±0.05) as a gate, or test on a latent scale fitted forward from single-entity dose-response cells at each level, or use lean's endpoint-normalised Phi with its bound.

confounds, overall rule: 'not supported' requires all six primaries to read absent or reversed. Sigma6 (planning MDE 400-800 tokens vs ±300 margin, plus a 'horizon too short' exit) and Sigma2 (0.26-0.66 vs ±0.3) sit at or above the 2x-margin 'underpowered' cut. The part can therefore practically not come out negative, against the design rule.

dynamics, feasibility: the core is 9.25 A100-h by its own count, above the 9-h envelope, with no pre-registered core trim order. Probe chunks at 28K are costed at 60 ms per 3 rows. HF's masked chunk path repeats K/V and DynamicCache rewrites the cache on every probe update, so a first-principles cost is about 0.2 s and the core becomes about 12.8 h with margin. The frozen plan is not executable within part D's budget.

dynamics, S2/S1 validity: (a) The pooled carry map m_(n+1) = f(m_n) has no item effects. Single-attractor items with heterogeneous fields can show two populated 'stable' zeros and s_c > 1 by aggregation, and G-D2pc plants no such case. (b) D3's per-item FPR (0.05) is calibrated on unimodal shapes only. A saturating probe of a diffusing entity, or a probe driven by the last answer's mention, gives U-shaped seed distributions, plausibly more so at long L0. 'Bistable carry map' and 'split grows with length' can therefore arise without any split.

lean (conditional; fixable): the D1-a null bound Phi <= 0.25 fails under a strong per-item word prior inside a saturating readout. At |b| >= 5 nats with saturation at 4-5 nats, Phi is 0.26-0.34 and rises as evidence weakens with length while endpoint retention stays >= 0.6, so G-deg passes. In that regime verdict 3 'length-driven minority capture' can arise from degradation plus prior. F-sym has no per-item closed-book check to exclude it.

confounds and dynamics, parity gates (conditional): 'max relative difference over logits < 1e-4' is ill-posed if computed per element, because near-zero logits make it fail whatever the engine does. Its failure voids every cache-reuse cell (confounds) or whole L0 levels (dynamics). Pin it to round-1 GO2's max|d|/max|x| or to nats on the readout tokens (as lean's G-LCE-1 does).
missing_everywhere: No design estimates the per-length readout response function: the single-entity log-odds dose-response over k = 1..n consistent records at each L, fitted forward. Without it, length effects cannot be tested on a latent evidence scale. Each design rests on an untested readout assumption that length-dependent saturation or degradation can break: an odd readout with no per-item prior (lean), log-additive pooling (confounds), or a unimodal readout of a unimodal latent with item-homogeneous maps (dynamics).

Filler-level clustering: only 3-4 filler documents per length, each shared by 4-12 items, while every bootstrap resamples items only. Filler-induced variance in the length contrasts thus rests on 3-4 draws, so intervals are too narrow, and the dynamics binomial and McNemar tests across items are not independent. Use one filler sample per item (about 5-20 extra A100-min of prefills) or a two-level bootstrap over filler documents and items.

No engine-failure fallback: in every design a failed cache/chunk parity gate voids the long-context cells. None pre-registers a full-recompute path (B = 1 full prefill per context, fewer items) that keeps the primary length contrast testable.

No design computes the probability that its overall rule reaches a decisive negative string under a plausible null (all required components adequately powered at once). The design rules require each part to be able to come out negative.
The rate form of hash share (which entity writes the next turn in self-continuation) never gets a verdict: lean has none, and dynamics and confounds report it descriptively or only in reserves.

No size or second-model comparison (for example Qwen3-0.6B, once its empty round-2 arm is explained) to calibrate how far a 1.7B null transfers. The persona and many-shot literature reports effects that grow with size. All three designs only state that a null does not refute H-DUAL for larger models.

falsifiers: D1-a reads 'no length-driven minority capture' (upper bound of Delta Phi < 0.03 with realized SD <= 0.012), 'majority sharpens with length', or 'length raises minority influence within proportional': no total-length effect beyond position and degradation (against part a)

D1-a reads 'not minority capture: explained by prior x saturation' (the effect lives only in the prior-aligned stratum), 'explained by conflict hedging' (a third-value minority produces the same length growth) or 'explained by filler form' (the effect needs coherent filler): the apparent capture is a known artifact (against part a)
D1-a reads 'minority over-representation without length dependence': a minority gets more than its share but length does not drive it (against the length claim only)
D1-b reads 'stable' or 'rises': the release threshold does not fall with total length at fixed positions (against the literal 'alpha* falls with L')
D1-c reads 'count-driven': in-context evidence accumulates like many-shot evidence, not like a hash-power share (against the share mapping)
D1-d reads 'no system cost': competition costs no coherence beyond a non-competing second entity (against the losing game)
D1-r reads 'token-identity-bound': the capture pattern changes under character-level encoding beyond +-0.07 (against 'the duality is not inside one token')

D3 reads 'no split at any length', 'split shrinks with length (urn-like)' or 'split at both lengths, no length trend': no force arising from hyper-long context splits one entity into two (against part b1)

D2-a reads 'competitor dilutes' or 'no catfish effect'; or D2-b 'weakens' or 'no length interaction'; or D2-c 'merging' or 'one entity captured': an opposed second entity does not keep the first going in a length-dependent way (against part b2, D2 member)

D5-a reads 'no lifetime effect of competition' or 'competition shortens coherence'; D5-x 'no full-scale advantage': two competing voices do not sustain their own text longer than two agreeing voices (against part b2, D5 member)
D4 reads 'absorbed into the role' or 'one blended entity' at 16K: no coexisting presented and retained identity (against catfishing as two entities from one)
D5-r reads 'no rate-form capture' or 'competing minority suppressed': a competing minority voice does not write more than its share beyond the turn-taking norm (against minority capture in rate form)

Combined: 'H-DUAL not supported in Qwen3-1.7B' when parts (a), (b1) and (b2) all read negative with gates passed (reached with probability 0.32-0.57 under a realistic null per simulation); never a refutation for larger models

Fatal flaw lean D1-a (both judges: per-item prior inside a saturating readout breaks Phi <= 0.25): neutral-note prior X_N per item-attribute at every length; prior-opposed stratum as a survival check (sim_strata_hedge.py: opposed stratum max 0.255 over 192 null grid points, aligned stratum up to 0.80); fitted forward null envelope env(L) from X_N, (0,5,5) and pure contexts (the per-length readout response function judge 2 found missing); G-D1-null validation on planted nulls; the false 'F-sym excludes prior fallback' claim removed; |b| strata reported.

Fatal flaw lean D1-c (judge 1: kappa pulled to 1.28-1.47 under saturated counting): replaced by equal-share (T1 vs T3) and equal-count-difference (T1 vs T2, judge 1's suggestion) contrasts with responsiveness guards T4 and pure (sim_countshare.py: counting r_sh -0.8 to -3.4, averaging -0.16 to +0.02; counting r_cs <= 0.40, averaging 0.56-0.71).

Fatal flaws of confounds (iota under saturation for Sigma1/Sigma3; D3c kappa slope; practically unreachable overall negative) and of dynamics (start in context for D1/D5; pooled carry map D2; cost and under-costed probe chunks): those measurements are not adopted. Only dynamics D3 and D6 and confounds D6/D7/C14/D3a/D3b/D8 are grafted, re-costed with judge 2's 0.2-s probe chunks at 28K; probe points limited to n = 0, 1, 6, 7, 8.

Dynamics D3 false positives under U-shaped, saturated and last-mention nulls (judge 2): per-seed mean over n = 6-8, persistence and gap criteria, and a conjunction with the in-context state readout. sim_split_v.py / sim_split_conj.py: probe-only rule fires on 0.63-0.87 of items under a saturated wide-latent null, the conjunction on 0.004; Beta(0.5,0.5) 0.15-0.25 and sticky last mention 0.20 remain, so the length trend decides; bar S >= 4 of 16.
Parity-gate formulation (judge 2: 'max relative difference < 1e-4' ill-posed): all parity gates in nats on the readout tokens (max 0.02, median 0.002) or by token identity.
